localChanges: Computer players now go for a space victory: once they know Computers they build the Apollo Program, research the advances a spaceship needs, build its parts in their best cities and launch it as Civilization's own computer players do, never with less than a 40% chance of arriving (closes #376).
A computer player with a spaceship in flight keeps an extra defender in its capital.
In games saved earlier, civilizations whose spaceships had ended up sharing one ship get one each again, and a part finished after a ship has launched no longer joins it.

log: A VictoryGoal has a weight and the advances it needs; goalFor picks the heaviest. ResearchForGoal researches the way to a goal's advances, found from the ruleset's Requirements rules. The space race (spaceRaceGoal, played by a SpaceRacePolicy) builds what gives a ship (BuildSpaceship), then its parts, and launches it (LaunchSpaceship). VictoryDependencies carries what these need beyond base-strategy-ai's Dependencies (civ-clone/web-renderer#376).

Review follow-ups: the probe's stand-ins are made with Object.create rather than new, so it no longer takes ids from each advance's class (a game would otherwise number its advances differently once the probe had run), and its cache is keyed on both registries.

Before 0.1.3 the Apollo Program gave every player's ship the same layout, so each player's parts went into everyone's ship. A Start rule now gives each ship still being built that shares its layout a layout of its own, with the parts its player's cities built; a ship in flight keeps what it launched with (civ-clone/web-renderer#376).

Parts still in production when a ship launched were added to it in flight, changing its flight time and chance of success after launch. They're now left behind, as a ship can't change in flight (civ-clone/web-renderer#376).

Review follow-ups (civ-clone/web-renderer#376): at a turn's start, a player whose ship is in flight stops building parts, which would only be left behind; a ship still being built that shares its layout with any other ship, launched or not, gets its own; and a player who came into the game after the Apollo Program was built (a civilization coming back, #178) gets a ship.
civ1-spaceship#2 moves the arrival check from Rules/Turn/start to Rules/Turn/end and gives the Apollo Program's ships to every player (civ-clone/web-renderer#177).

civ1-science's repeatable Future Technology (civ-clone/web-renderer#458) is on offer to a player who knows nearly everything, which every ChooseResearch test's player does, so it crowded out the advances each test is about (civ-clone/web-renderer#66).

Once a player knows Computers, or has a ship with parts on it, it plays for space (base-strategy-victory): it researches Space Flight, Plastics and Robotics, builds the Apollo Program in its most productive city, then a ship in balanced steps in its most productive third of cities, and launches by v474.05's rules: never under a 40% chance; when the ship is complete, better than 75%, outranked, or a rival's ship would arrive no sooner; not while no rival knows Space Flight. Ours on top: a complete ship, or one that would otherwise arrive within 10 years of the final year, launches. A capital keeps a defender more while its ship is in flight (civ-clone/web-renderer#376).

Review follow-ups: a Propulsion waits for its Fuel, not the frame, so it no longer asks for a Structural, and none is wanted once the frame has no room; a city still wanting defenders builds those before the Apollo Program or parts; and science doesn't stop while a player playing for space lacks an advance its ship needs (civ-clone/web-renderer#376).
